Definition: from G1487 and G4458; if somehow:--if by any means.
BiblicalUsage: This phrase means if by any means, and Paul uses it for the hopes he holds lightly and prays about. He prays that by any means he might come to Rome, that by any means he might provoke his fellow Jews to jealousy and save some, and that by any means he might attain to the resurrection of the dead. The phrase is the sound of a man who will take any road God opens.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe if by any means is honest praying, because Paul did not demand his road, he asked for any road that led where God wanted him.
